intent.primaryUser: A platform operator or architect who wants to see how the platform is wired together.
intent.triggeringNeed: Understanding or demonstrating the breadth of what the platform knows about itself — source code, data model, knowledge corpus, architecture, infrastructure, and business portfolio — which was only possible through the Neo4j browser before BET-5 retired it.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_admin capability.
The graph mirror has been populated by the code-graph indexer, the EA/discovery sync, and the knowledge/portfolio backfill.
intent.job: Find a starting point in the corpus and follow its relationships outward to see what it connects to.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name a thing (a file, a data model, a route, a tool, an EA element), see its neighbourhood drawn, and read its properties and degree.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Graph Explorer' item in the Advanced family, alongside Platform Development.

deferredRegions.role: Per-label and per-relationship-type facets with live counts.
Raw property map for one node.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator clicks a node on the canvas.

familyConsistency.terminology: Operator-facing names throughout — 'Source file', 'Data model', 'Route' — never the raw storage labels stored in graph_node.labels.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Search and depth controls sit above the canvas; per-node actions sit in the right-hand inspector.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (searching, loading, clipped-view notice) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Four choices by default (domain, search, hops, expand); the 12 node labels and 15 relationship types stay behind 'Advanced filters'.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Reset returns the surface to the census-only state without leaving the route.

empty-corpus.statePredicate: The graph mirror has no rows.
empty-corpus.completionSignal: The census reads zero nodes and zero relationships.
empty-corpus.errorCorrection: The operator runs the code-graph indexer or discovery sync to populate the mirror.

no-starting-point.statePredicate: The corpus is populated but the operator has not chosen a seed node.
no-starting-point.completionSignal: Search results list at least one candidate starting point.
no-starting-point.errorCorrection: An unmatched query explains that nothing matched and suggests a shorter fragment or clearing the domain filter.

neighbourhood-drawn.statePredicate: A seed node is selected and its neighbourhood has loaded.
neighbourhood-drawn.completionSignal: The canvas draws the seed and its neighbours, and the inspector shows the clicked node's labels, properties, and degree.
neighbourhood-drawn.errorCorrection: A clipped view states the node cap and names the three ways to narrow it — relationship filter, node-type filter, or fewer hops.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find the BacklogItem data model in the graph and tell me how many relationships it has.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The inspector shows the BacklogItem node with the Data model label and a relationship count.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a count from the corpus census tiles instead of the node inspector.
The canvas renders but the inspector is never opened, so no per-node evidence is read.
A clipped view is mistaken for the node's complete neighbourhood.
acceptanceThresholds: The starting point is found within three search attempts.
No raw storage label (for example ArchiMate__DataObject) is shown to the operator.
Rendered subgraphs stay within the node cap so the canvas remains interactive.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Operator asked for the Neo4j-style visual graph exploration capability to return, under Admin, for exploring and demonstrating the corpus and code graph.
BET-5 mirrored the Neo4j graph into graph_node / graph_edge with the same traversal surface, but shipped no visual explorer over it.

intent.primaryUser: An HR or recruiting operator with the view_employee capability.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing the whole recruiting funnel across natively-created applications and Greenhouse-sourced candidates as one list — without logging into two systems or reconciling duplicates by hand.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_employee capability (the Employee area gate).
Recruiting data exists: native Applications and/or Greenhouse-staged application records imported through the connector.
intent.job: Scan the unified recruiting funnel, read how many candidates are native versus sourced-from-Greenhouse-and-not-yet-promoted, see the shape by stage, and narrow to a single requisition.
intent.successOutcome: The operator sees one deduped funnel, reads the native / Greenhouse / total counts and the by-stage summary, can filter to a single requisition, and can tell a native candidate from a Greenhouse-sourced one at a glance.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Recruiting' entry in the Employee area, beside the People directory.

familyConsistency.terminology: Candidate display names and source labels ('Native', 'Greenhouse') — never raw external ids or connector internals.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: The requisition filter sits above the candidate list; changing it re-reads the funnel in place.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline pending state on the list while the filtered funnel re-reads — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Counts, stage summary, and the full funnel show by default; the requisition filter narrows the same list rather than revealing a new surface.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Selecting 'All requisitions' restores the full funnel without leaving the route.

empty-funnel.statePredicate: No native Applications and no un-promoted Greenhouse-staged rows exist.
empty-funnel.completionSignal: The count trio reads zero and an empty-state message explains that native and Greenhouse-sourced candidates will appear here as they arrive.
empty-funnel.errorCorrection: The empty state names both sources so the operator knows nothing is hidden — the funnel is genuinely empty, not mis-filtered.

populated-funnel.statePredicate: At least one native Application or un-promoted Greenhouse-staged row exists.
populated-funnel.completionSignal: Each candidate row shows a source badge (Native or Greenhouse), stage, and status; the counts and stage chips reconcile with the list.
populated-funnel.errorCorrection: A candidate imported from Greenhouse and already promoted appears once (native), never twice — the crosswalk dedupe is visible in the counts.

filtered-empty.statePredicate: A requisition is selected but has no applications in the funnel.
filtered-empty.completionSignal: The list is empty and the message points to clearing the requisition filter to see the full funnel.
filtered-empty.errorCorrection: The empty state distinguishes 'this requisition has no candidates' from 'the funnel is empty' so the operator clears the filter rather than concluding recruiting is idle.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Show me the recruiting funnel and tell me how many candidates came from Greenhouse but haven't been promoted to native yet.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator reads the 'From Greenhouse' count and can point to Greenhouse-badged rows in the list.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator counts a promoted (native) candidate as a Greenhouse one.
The requisition filter is mistaken for a search over all candidates rather than a narrowing to one role.
An empty filtered list is read as an empty funnel.
acceptanceThresholds: Native and Greenhouse-sourced candidates are distinguishable at a glance via the source badge.
The funnel counts reconcile with the visible list.
The page performs no write action — it is a read-only funnel.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder selected the visual recruiting pipeline page as the next absorption chunk and signed off an HTML prototype: a read-only funnel with count trio, by-stage summary, source-badged candidate list, and a requisition filter.

getRecruitingPipeline already merges native Applications with Greenhouse-staged rows and dedupes via the MasterDataSourceRef crosswalk; the coworker tool (BI-E64D11AE) surfaces it to the AI workforce. This page is its human-facing surface, reading the same model so the two never drift.

intent.primaryUser: A platform operator supervising the AI coworker workforce.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing what the AI coworkers are doing right now and what they got done today — and where nobody is acting — without leaving to read logs or opening HR-sensitive records.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_platform capability.
The workforce roster is seeded and coworkers have produced TaskRun / ToolExecution / TokenUsage activity.
intent.job: Scan the coworker workforce, see who is active and what they accomplished, and spot idle coworkers or missing human owners.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name which coworkers are working, read each one's outcomes for the day, see the responsible human, and notice where activity is absent — all as aggregate signals, never sensitive record content.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Right Now' tab beside Workforce and Operations Map.

deferredRegions.role: Per-coworker manage jump-offs (settings, priority and models, skills and grants, schedule).

familyConsistency.terminology: Coworker-facing names and business outcomes — '3 PRs opened', 'employee records updated' — never raw tool names.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Manage jump-offs sit on each coworker row; refresh sits in the freshness bar above the roster.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (refreshing, last-updated age) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Working and quiet coworkers show by default; per-coworker management stays behind 'Manage'.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Refresh re-fetches the snapshot in place without leaving the route.

all-idle.statePredicate: No coworker has an active or waiting TaskRun.
all-idle.completionSignal: The Working-now list is empty and the quiet list shows every coworker with its last-acted age.
all-idle.errorCorrection: An empty working list states that no coworker is active and points to the quiet list for how long each has been idle.

active-work.statePredicate: At least one coworker has a live TaskRun.
active-work.completionSignal: Each working coworker shows its current task, today's outcome chips, tokens, and responsible human.
active-work.errorCorrection: Sensitive-data activity renders as an aggregate flag with no drill-in, so no record content is exposed to a non-HR operator.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Tell me which coworker did the most today and who is responsible for it.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator names a coworker from the Working-now list with its outcome chips and reads its human owner.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a coworker name from the idle roster instead of the working list.
Sensitive record content is expected instead of the aggregate count and flag.
Token totals are mistaken for accomplishment outcomes.
acceptanceThresholds: No sensitive record content is shown to a non-HR operator.
Idle coworkers are distinguishable from working ones at a glance.
Each coworker's human owner (or its absence) is legible.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder asked for a workforce view showing what AI coworkers are doing and have accomplished, with inactivity as a signal, sensitive-data as an aggregate flag only, and the responsible human surfaced.
The Operations Map already loads TaskRun / ToolExecution / TokenUsage but presents them as an analytical topology/replay surface, not a workforce-activity roster.

intent.primaryUser: A platform operator looking at one AI coworker as a first-class identity, the way they look at a person or a customer.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing everything about one AI coworker in a single place — what it does and why it's valuable, who has engaged it, what it costs, and its skills — and adjusting how it behaves, without hopping across platform-admin surfaces.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_platform capability (managing behaviour dials additionally requires manage_platform).
The coworker exists in the workforce registry.
intent.job: Inspect a coworker's identity — definition, engagements, cost, skills — and set its priority and proactivity in place.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can state what the coworker does and why it's here, see which people and other agents have engaged it, read what it has cost, and change its Cost/Quality/Time priority and proactivity from this one surface.

findability.discoveryCue: Selecting a coworker from the roster opens its identity.

deferredRegions.role: The Cost/Quality/Time priority control (Golden Triangle + inheritance).
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator activates 'Change' on the Priority setting.

deferredRegions.role: The Quiet/Balanced/Assertive proactivity control and its runtime effects.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator activates 'Change' on the Proactivity setting.

deferredRegions.role: Full facet bodies (cost drivers, engagement list, skills).
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator opens a collapsed facet summary.

familyConsistency.terminology: Coworker-facing role names and plain-language outcomes — 'who has engaged it', 'what it cost' — never raw tool names or agent ids.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Ask and Manage sit in the identity header; behaviour dials sit directly below the at-a-glance band; each facet expands in place.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (the priority control's saving/saved line) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Definition and the at-a-glance summary show by default; settings show only their current value until 'Change'; facets show a one-line summary until opened.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Expanding a facet or a dial reveals detail in place without leaving the route; 'Manage' deep-links to the admin record for edits beyond the dials.

no-activity.statePredicate: The coworker has no recorded engagements and no recorded spend in the window.
no-activity.completionSignal: The definition and at-a-glance band render; the engagements and cost facets state plainly that nothing has been recorded yet.
no-activity.errorCorrection: An empty engagements facet states that no one has engaged the coworker yet, rather than showing a blank region.

has-activity.statePredicate: The coworker has recorded engagements and/or spend in the window.
has-activity.completionSignal: The engagements facet distinguishes people from other agents with recency; the cost facet shows spend, trend, drivers, and budget posture.
has-activity.errorCorrection: A read hiccup on cost or engagements fails open to an empty-state facet rather than 500-ing the identity.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Tell me what this coworker does, who has engaged it, and what it has cost — then set its priority to Quality first.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator reads the definition, names a person and an agent that engaged it, reads the 30-day cost, and changes the priority to Quality first.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a raw agentId instead of the role name.
Token totals are mistaken for accomplishment or for dollar cost.
The operator leaves to the admin record to read cost or engagements that belong on the identity.
acceptanceThresholds: The definition (what it does / why valuable) is legible at the top without scrolling into a facet.
People and other agents that engaged it are visually distinguishable.
Priority and proactivity are changeable in place, showing inheritance / current value first.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder asked for a single place to see an AI coworker as an identity (definition, engagements, costs, skills) and drill in — the way People and Customers work — for employees and other AI use-cases.

The admin coworker record already aggregates the coworker's facets but is positioned as platform administration; this identity surface reuses its loader and the canonical priority/proactivity controls.
